reviews.t: It works! And no more dried out nails
reviews.x: I was a bit skeptical that this would work, but I bought it HOPING it would work.  AND IT DOES!  My fingernails have five coats total of base, polish and topcoat, so it is a bit of work to remove my nail polish irrespective of what I use for remover.  This remover did as good of a job as traditional nail polish remover at clearing all of those layers from my nails.  I found that I had to squish the remover around on my nails (after it sat for a few minutes) in order to get all of the polish off.

This was a great buy as I have been on the lookout for a 100% natural nail polish remover. This product is just as effective as traditional nail polish removers, but without the toxic smell. claims.text: Most reviewers find it works well, often as effectively as acetone, including on regular and gel polish.
Many praise the mild, plant-based scent compared to harsh acetone.
Some reviewers report it does not work well, especially on glitter polish, and requires patience.
Several reviewers note it is gentler on nails and skin than acetone.
A few reviewers raise concerns about packaging (glass bottle/dropper) and an undisclosed soy ingredient.

qa.q: How long does it take to see results?
qa.answer: Reviews describe removal taking longer than acetone, with some saying it takes a couple of minutes per nail [1][3], while others report it not working at all [2][4].

claims.text: It takes longer to remove polish than with acetone.
Some had to work each nail a couple of minutes each.
Some reviewers report it did not successfully remove polish.

qa.q: Does it actually work on toenail fungus?
qa.answer: Not enough evidence in reviews to answer this.

qa.q: How do I apply it and how often?
qa.answer: Apply it with a cotton pad or cotton ball, making sure the nail looks wet, then wait a few minutes before wiping or gently rubbing off the polish [2][5]. Reviews don't specify a fixed frequency; one reviewer notes it may take a couple minutes per nail [6].

claims.text: Use a cotton pad or cotton ball to apply it to each nail and make sure the nail looks wet [2][5].
Wait a few minutes, then use the soaked pad or gently rub to remove the polish [2][5].
It may take a couple minutes per nail [6].

qa.q: Does it have a strong smell?
qa.answer: Reviews disagree on smell: some say it has no strong or harsh chemical smell [1][2][3][4], but one notes it "does not have a nice smell" [2].
